summary: Reserved pool latency drift and elevated timeouts correlated with nightly background maintenance jobs
description:
Issue summary:
BrightDocs reports elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 504 timeouts from their Dedicated reservation beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. The impact aligns with our cluster nightly maintenance window (22:00-23:30 UTC).

Impact:
- Customer-visible: increased request latency (p95 up from ~120ms to 1.1s, p99 spikes to 3.4s) and 504s for synchronous streaming requests.
- Affects production traffic for BrightDocs' reserved capacity in us-west-2 (dedicated pool ID: dp-56f9).
- Business impact: degraded UX during evening peak for customer; BrightDocs billing tier and SLAs flagged this as P1.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-56f9 (3 reserved nodes, GPU: A10G equivalent), auto-scale policy: min=3 max=6 scale_cooldown=300s, preemptible=false.
- Node image: node-agent-v2.14.1 (includes nightly maintenance agent).
- Models in use when issue observed: redwood-2.7b (chat), mistral-7b (reranking).

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) Customer runs bursty workloads starting ~2026-03-09 21:45 UTC.
2) At ~22:00 UTC nightly maintenance jobs begin (node-agent orchestrates OS package updates, kernel GC, background log rotation and node-level checkpoint consolidation).
3) Within ~5-12 minutes of maintenance start, telemetry shows increased scheduler queue length and longer wait times for GPU contexts.
4) Customers see streaming disconnects and 504s; requests are retried by client at higher rates which amplifies the queue.

Logs / Metrics (examples):
- grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serve/dedicated-pool-dp-56f9?orgId=1&from=2026-03-09T21:30:00Z&to=2026-03-09T23:30:00Z
- p95 latency (redwood-2.7b): baseline ~120ms -> spike to 1.1s at 22:07 UTC.
- p99 latency: baseline ~450ms -> spikes 3.4s, correlates with GPU context switch rate increase.
- node_exporter: write_iops spikes on /var/lib/checkpoints starting 22:02 UTC.
- nvidia_smi: transient GPU utilization drop and higher kernel launch latency reported on node-03 which is running the maintenance agent.

Expected behavior:
- Nightly maintenance should not interfere with serving-critical processes on reserved nodes; scheduling should prefer off-host maintenance or drain with graceful workload evacuation.

Additional notes:
- Customer has routing pinned to pool dp-56f9. Failover routing to other pools is possible but not enabled in their config.
- Similar timing pattern has been observed in other reserved pools in us-west during the same maintenance window (see linked issues).
comments: 2026-03-10 02:12 — Support (Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after BrightDocs support call at 23:00 UTC. Collected initial logs and confirmed correlation with nightly maintenance window.

2026-03-10 03:05 — SRE (Marco Li): Confirmed increased queue length and GPU context latency on node-03. Noted disk IO activity on /var/lib/checkpoints concurrent with spike. Hypothesis: maintenance agent performing checkpoint consolidation is contending for CPU/io and causing kernel/GPU latency.

2026-03-10 05:20 — Customer (BrightDocs - Emma Zhou): Provided request traces and mentioned they did not configure cross-pool fallback because they wanted data locality. Asking for mitigation options tonight.

2026-03-10 07:40 — Platform Eng (Diego Morales): Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) disable nightly maintenance on dp-56f9 for next 24 hours, 2) temporarily increase min nodes to 4 to provide headroom, 3) enable routing fallback to regional shared pool. Preparing an autoscaler patch to reduce cooldown acceleration during eviction events.
2026-03-10 09:15 — SRE (Marco Li): Actioned temporary disable of maintenance on dp-56f9 (change-id CHG-7882), increased min nodes to 4. Monitoring for next maintenance window.

2026-03-12 11:02 — Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirmed improved p95 and no 504s during subsequent maintenance window after mitigations. Follow-up engineering work assigned for root cause and permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Telemetry aggregated from Grafana and node logs indicates the main contention vector is node-level IO and scheduler preemption during checkpoint consolidation; this increases kernel launch latency observable in CUDA profiler traces.
nvprof sample (node-03, 2026-03-09T22:05): average kernel launch latency increased 6x vs baseline; GPU occupancy transiently drops suggesting CPU-side stalls rather than GPU load saturation.
Autoscaler behavior: min=3, observed burst increased active pods but autoscaler cooldown prevented quick scale up while nodes were blocked by maintenance-related IO, causing queue to back up.
Hypothesis 1: maintenance agent not respecting cgroup/ionice limits, performing high-priority IO on shared checkpoint disk, causing host CPU and I/O contention and delaying serving threads.

Hypothesis 2: node-agent triggers lightweight local checkpoint compaction on same disk backing model cache; compaction uses synchronous fsyncs that block the serving process's pagefault handling, increasing kernel scheduling latency.
Reproducibility: reproduced in staging by enabling maintenance job on a 3-node reserved pool while running a synthetic bursty workload; observed same p95/p99 drift within 6-10 minutes.
Cross-reference: SUP-642113 observed similar p99 patterns but was attributed to vram paging; this ticket differs because we see host IO spikes rather than GPU OOM activity.

Action items taken so far: disabled maintenance on customer pool for 48h, bumped min nodes to 4, queued autoscaler config change (PR referenced) to allow faster scale up when queue depth exceeds threshold.
Next step: instrument node-agent to respect ionice and CPU shares and implement a 'maintenance-drain' mode that triggers graceful evac prior to IO-intensive work.
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-10): Disabled nightly maintenance on dp-56f9 (CHG-7882), increased pool min nodes to 4 to provide immediate headroom, and offered enablement of routing fallback to BrightDocs. Customer accepted these temporary mitigations.

Permanent fix (planned): 1) Update node-agent to run background consolidation at low IO priority (ionice -c3) and within a cpuset/cgroup that avoids core serving processes. 2) Implement maintenance-drain mode that sets node to cordon and migrates active contexts before heavy IO. 3) Adjust autoscaler thresholds so scale-up can preempt maintenance windows if queue depth rises rapidly. 4) Add a monitoring alert for 'maintenance+queue correlation' to auto-trigger mitigations.

Deployment plan: node-agent change scheduled for canary on 2026-03-18, full rollout 2026-03-25 after performance validation. Autoscaler tuning PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/98 (in review).
Follow-up: Postmortem and runbook update to be published to Confluence (link to be added). Assign owners: Diego Morales (node-agent), Priya Raman (autoscaler).
